messages:
oncall-bot: PagerDuty notice: trigger INC-2026-09-3129 fired for service=redwood-inference-api (p95 latency > 1.2s, 503 rate > 4%) in us-west-2. Root cause suspected after recent rollout v2026.3. Auto-page to SRE rotation. 

pd-bot: PagerDuty: page assigned to @sre-jordan. Escalation timer started (10m). Link: https://pd.example/INC-2026-09-3129

sre-jordan: Acked the page. grabbing logs now. Can someone confirm what went out in v2026.3? @deploy-bot what changed?

deploy-bot: Rollout v2026.3: encoder refactor + KV-cache pruning enabled behind ff:encoder_v2=true, traffic split 10% -> 100% over 30m. No infra changes.

eng-elena: I see a spike of 503s from the dedicated inference pool (kube ns=redwood-dedicated-usw2). Stack traces point at the encoder module NPE during warmup. Sending sample stack: ```
java.lang.NullPointerException at com.redwood.encoder.V2Warmup.initialize(Encoder.java:132)
```

support-anya: Support channels: ~18 customer errors reported in last 8m, several enterprise requests timeout on generation endpoint. CS flagged two paying customers with active sessions.

product-liam: Not good. Need quick mitigation and customer-facing ETA. Prioritize minimizing blast radius over partial fixes.

sre-jordan: Agreed. Starting staged rollback of encoder_v2. Steps: 1) flip feature flag to false for us-west-2 canary 2) scale down new pods 3) divert 100% traffic back to v2026.2 if flag flip doesn't stabilize in 3m. Executing flag toggle now.

sre-jordan: ```bash
# disable new encoder flag for region-specific rollout
curl -X POST https://flags.redwood/api/toggle -H 'Authorization: Bearer $FLAG_OPS' -d '{"flag":"encoder_v2","region":"us-west-2","value":false}'
```

deploy-bot: flag toggle API accepted, change id f-0a9b. Propagating.

eng-elena: Metrics already improving on canary pods (error rate down from 6.8% -> 1.7%). Observability: https://grafana.redwood/d/encoder/rollouts?panel=errors&range=15m

pd-bot: PagerDuty: escalation suppressed (acknowledged). Next escalation at +20m if no resolution.

sre-jordan: Running `kubectl rollout undo deploy/encoder-service -n redwood-dedicated-usw2 --to-revision=2026.2` on canary subset, then will roll the rest if green.

sre-jordan: ```
# undo canary deployment
kubectl -n redwood-dedicated-usw2 set image deploy/encoder-service encoder=registry/redwood/encoder:2026.2 --selector=rollout=canary
```

eng-elena: Canary pods restarted on 2026.2, CPU and memory look normal. No more NPEs in recent logs. p95 latency trending back to baseline.

support-anya: Notified the two customers directly: shared that we're mitigating and will follow-up with a postmortem. No escalations from their side so far.

product-liam: Please prepare a short status note for customers: what happened, who was impacted, mitigation steps, and next steps for rollback verification and postmortem.

sre-jordan: Will prepare. Current status: Incident mitigated for us-west-2 after flag toggle and canary rollback. Will continue to monitor for 30m before rolling changes to other regions. PD still open until we're stable.

oncall-bot: Reminder: run incident checklist: triage notes, timeline, metrics snapshots, and attach logs to INC-2026-09-3129.

deploy-bot: Queued full rollback to 2026.2 for remaining hosts in us-west-2, will pause if any regressions.

eng-elena: Quick post-check: KV-cache hit ratio unchanged; root cause looks purely code-path in encoder_v2 warmup. Plan: revert encoder warmup refactor, run unit/infra canary, re-roll with tighter ff gates.

product-liam: Good plan. After stabilization, schedule a short postmortem sync with SRE/ENG/PM/Support tomorrow.

sre-jordan: Closing loop here — incident remains ACKED but mitigated. I’ll follow up in INC and create initial timeline. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

pd-bot: PagerDuty: incident INC-2026-09-3129 remains active (acknowledged). No further escalation unless error rate > 3% persist.

support-anya: Adding customer notes and ticket links to the incident.

sre-jordan: (final) marking as \"mitigated — rollback in progress\". Will update last_message_ts when we close.
